title: Microsoft Is Quietly Deleting 32 GB RAM Recommendation for Windows 11
excerpt: Microsoft is retroactively removing documentation from its website and materials that mention 32 GB of RAM as a recommendation for new PC builds or purchases. Instead, the company is now emphasizing 8 GB devices that are optimized to run Windows 11 smoothly, even with that RAM configuration....
content_html:
Microsoft is retroactively removing documentation from its website and materials that mention 32 GB of RAM as a recommendation for new PC builds or purchases. Instead, the company is now emphasizing 8 GB devices that are optimized to run Windows 11 smoothly, even with that RAM configuration. Thanks to Windows Latest, which spotted the changes, Microsoft's Windows Learning Center has been updated to remove mentions of the 32 GB RAM recommendation. Previously, Microsoft published a document suggesting that 16 GB is a baseline for a modern PC, describing it as a good "starting point." However, the company also used to recommend that gamers try to surpass this baseline, suggesting 32 GB as a "no worries" upgrade for gaming PCs.

At that time, this sparked significant controversy as gamers were vocal about Microsoft recommending more RAM when purchasing additional memory could cost as much as an entire PC, depending on the configuration. Amid a severe DRAM shortage, Microsoft faced pushback from gamers and quietly removed the mention of the 32 GB "no worries" recommendation. This also raised concerns about whether Microsoft would optimize the Windows 11 operating system to perform better on lower-spec PCs with less than 16 GB of RAM, such as the 8 GB PCs that Microsoft sells itself, like the Surface Pro 12 and Surface Laptop 13, both of which come with 8 GB base configurations.

We already know that the company is overhauling many components within its Windows 11 operating system. Microsoft has made substantial improvements in memory efficiency and latency to accelerate the modernization of Windows 11. It has reduced memory overhead across apps and components and has optimized WinUI 3 to make built-in apps use less memory. Microsoft also outlined its plans for future Windows 11 memory efficiency improvements, specifically stating that the Windows team will be working on "memory optimization for 8 GB and above." As a result, the company has removed recommendations and mentions of 32 GB RAM from its documents and websites to avoid additional pushback.

content_html_zh:
Microsoft 正在追溯性地从其网站中删除提及 32 GB RAM 作为新 PC 构建或购买建议的文档和材料。 相反，该公司现在强调 8 GB 设备，即使采用这种 RAM 配置，也能顺利运行 Windows 11。 感谢 Windows Latest 发现了这些变化，微软的 Windows 学习中心已经更新，删除了 32 GB RAM 建议的提及。 此前，微软发布了一份文件，建议16GB是现代PC的基线，并将其描述为一个很好的“起点”。 不过，该公司也曾建议游戏玩家尝试超越这一基准，建议 32 GB 作为游戏 PC 的“无忧”升级。

当时，这引发了重大争议，因为游戏玩家强烈反对微软推荐更多 RAM，因为购买额外内存的成本可能相当于整台 PC（具体取决于配置）。 在 DRAM 严重短缺的情况下，微软面临游戏玩家的反对，悄悄删除了 32 GB“无忧”建议的提及。 这也引发了人们的担忧，即微软是否会优化 Windows 11 操作系统，使其在 RAM 低于 16 GB 的低规格 PC 上表现更好，例如微软自己销售的 8 GB 电脑，例如 Surface Pro 12 和 Surface Laptop 13，这两款电脑都配备了 8 GB 基本配置。

我们已经知道该公司正在对其 Windows 11 操作系统中的许多组件进行彻底修改。 微软在内存效率和延迟方面进行了大幅改进，以加速 Windows 11 的现代化。 它减少了应用程序和组件的内存开销，并优化了 WinUI 3，使内置应用程序使用更少的内存。 微软还概述了未来 Windows 11 内存效率改进的计划，特别指出 Windows 团队将致力于“8 GB 及以上的内存优化”。 因此，该公司已从其文档和网站中删除了有关 32 GB RAM 的建议和提及，以避免进一步的抵制。
